title: A methodological approach to the air-sea energy fluxes data collection and analysis at the tropical coastal ocean
author: Yusup, Kayode, et al.

steps.title: Install Eddy Covariance System
steps.instruction: Mount the eddy covariance system on a stable stainless‑steel platform extending the existing pier at the Muka Head station (5°28′6″N, 100°12′1″E) so it is directly over the ocean; place the 3‑D sonic anemometer (model 81000 V, RM Young) and the open‑path CO₂/H₂O gas analyzer (model LI‑7500 A, LI‑COR) at 4.1 m above the sea surface; factory‑calibrate both sensors before deployment; connect them to a LI‑7550 Analyzer Interface Unit data logger and set the recording frequency to 20 Hz; configure the system to average fluxes in 30‑min blocks and adopt the convention that negative flux values indicate downward movement while positive values indicate upward movement.

substeps.instruction: Mount platform at specified coordinates.
Install sonic anemometer and gas analyzer at 4.1 m height.
Factory‑calibrate sensors.
Connect sensors to LI‑7550 logger and set 20 Hz sampling.
Set 30‑min averaging and flux sign convention.

steps.title: Deploy Complementary Biomet Sensors
steps.instruction: Install the Biomet slow‑response suite: atmospheric temperature/relative humidity sensor (model HMP155, Vaisala; TA accuracy ±0.7 °C, RH accuracy ±1.7 %); pyranometer for global radiation (model LI‑200SL, LI‑COR; error <5 %); net radiometer (model NR LITE 2, Kipp & Zonen; sensitivity 13.6 µV W⁻¹ m⁻²); two LI‑COR thermistors at 0.5 m depth (TS1) and 2.5 m depth (TS2) (accuracy ±1 °C); factory‑calibrate all sensors; connect them to a Sutron 9210b Xlite data logger set to record at 1 min intervals and average to 30‑min blocks; retrieve cumulative 15‑min precipitation data from the nearby Davis Vantage Pro2 Plus station IPENANGP2 (5°28′4″N, 100°17′25″E).

substeps.instruction: Install TA/RH sensor, pyranometer, net radiometer, and thermistors at specified depths.
Factory‑calibrate each sensor.
Wire sensors to the 9210b Xlite logger and set 1 min sampling.
Configure logger to produce 30‑min averages.
Obtain 15‑min precipitation totals from the IPENANGP2 station.

steps.title: Process Raw 20‑Hz Data
steps.instruction: Import the raw 20 Hz eddy covariance data into EddyPro Version 6 (LI‑COR); apply the following filters: amplitude resolution, spike removal, dropout correction, absolute limits, skewness, and kurtosis; perform the two‑fold rotation tilt‑correction on the sonic anemometer to force the mean vertical wind speed to zero; carry out footprint estimation as described in the referenced method.

substeps.instruction: Load data into EddyPro v6.
Apply amplitude resolution filter.
Remove spikes and dropouts.
Enforce absolute limits, check skewness and kurtosis.
Execute two‑fold rotation tilt correction.
Estimate flux footprint.

steps.title: Quality‑Flag Flux Data
steps.instruction: Within EddyPro run the steady‑state test and the developed‑turbulence conditions test; assign quality flags (0 = best, 1 = good, 2 = bad) and discard all records with flag 2; compute the ratio σw/u* (σw = standard deviation of vertical wind speed, u* = friction velocity) and retain only data for wind directions 0°–90° where the ratio holds (typical ocean‑facing sector); discard data from directions 90°–360°; note that after these filters 21 % of LE and H data remain; do not fill any gaps in the dataset.

substeps.instruction: Run steady‑state and turbulence‑condition tests.
Flag data (0, 1, 2) and remove flag 2 records.
Calculate σw/u* and keep data for 0°–90° wind directions.
Discard data for 90°–360° directions.
Record that 21 % of LE and H data are retained.
Leave all gaps unfilled.

steps.title: Filter Wind Speed and Temperature Gaps
steps.instruction: Exclude wind speed records outside the 0°–90° sector that also deviate from the expected σw/u* ratio of approximately 1.3; discard TS1 temperature records that show extreme values caused by sensor failure (notably the gap from August to mid‑September); retain all other Biomet and precipitation measurements.

substeps.instruction: Remove wind speed data outside 0°–90° with σw/u* ≠ 1.3.
Delete TS1 data gaps (August‑mid‑September) caused by sensor breakdown.

steps.title: Summarize Turbulent Heat Fluxes
steps.instruction: Calculate half‑hourly latent heat (LE) flux range (−36 W m⁻² to 130 W m⁻²) and sensible heat (H) flux range (−12 W m⁻² to 24 W m⁻²); compute mean half‑hourly LE (11.67 W m⁻²) and H (1.56 W m⁻²); determine the Bowen ratio H/LE (0.13).

steps.title: Summarize Underwater Temperature
steps.instruction: Determine temperature ranges at TS1 (0.5 m) and TS2 (2.5 m) of 27 °C to 33 °C; calculate mean temperatures: TS1 = 30.85 °C, TS2 = 30.27 °C; note that TS1 may be exposed during low tide, leading to occasional higher readings; acknowledge that TS1 data gaps (August‑mid‑September) were removed.

steps.title: Summarize Radiation Measurements
steps.instruction: Record half‑hourly global radiation (RG) range 0 W m⁻² to 1020 W m⁻² and net radiation (RN) range −130 W m⁻² to 990 W m⁻²; note peak average values in mid‑March: RG ≈ 217 W m⁻², RN ≈ 163 W m⁻².

steps.title: Summarize Air Temperature & Humidity
steps.instruction: Report air temperature variation from 22 °C to 32 °C and relative humidity variation from 50 % to 100 %; highlight higher daytime temperatures and larger fluctuations during precipitation events.
